events.title: Pascal language report published
events.summary: Niklaus Wirth published The Programming Language Pascal at ETH Zurich — a structured teaching language built on ALGOL 60.
events.about: Pascal was designed for teaching programming and writing clear, structured code on small machines. It introduced records, sets, and strong typing in a compact language. Turbo Pascal on the IBM PC, UCSD Pascal on Apple II, and decades of CS101 courses made it the default intro language before Java and Python.

narrative.whyChosen: Wirth wanted a small, learnable language that still scaled to real programs — fewer concepts than PL/I, more structure than BASIC.
narrative.whyImportant: Pascal popularized structured programming (no goto), influenced Modula-2 and Ada, and trained a generation of programmers.
narrative.problemSolved: ALGOL 60 was elegant but hard to implement; PL/I was huge. Pascal hit a sweet spot for education and efficient one-pass compilation.

sources.title: Wirth — The Programming Language Pascal (ETH report, November 1970)
